[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of interventions combining dietary protein timing and resistance exercise for lean mass preservation during weight loss in older adults. — Synthesizes existing evidence to assess consistency and effect size across studies, which can confirm or refute the hypothesis at a higher level of evidence.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical model of muscle protein synthesis dynamics: interaction between protein ingestion timing, anabolic resistance in aging, and resistance training-induced sensitization. — Provides mechanistic plausibility and identifies key variables (e.g., per-meal protein dose, training intensity) that could explain why the combination might be superior, guiding refinement of the hypothesis.

qualifier.comparison: compared to caloric restriction with protein-matched meal timing alone

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of existing studies on meal timing and protein distribution in caloric restriction interventions for older adults. — Synthesizing available evidence can clarify whether any impact is consistently observed across studies, addressing the current low confidence.

C007.subject: Caloric restriction with protein-matched meal timing
C007.object: fat-free mass preservation in older adults when daily protein is skewed toward the evening meal
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Caloric restriction with protein-matched meal timing fat-free mass preservation in older adults when daily protein is skewed toward the evening meal]

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing older adults on caloric restriction with protein skewed to evening vs. evenly distributed, measuring fat-free mass via DXA or MRI at 0, 6, and 12 months. — Directly tests the hypothesis in the target population and timeframe, providing causal evidence on whether evening-skewed protein impairs fat-free mass preservation.

[PATH:empirical] Mechanistic study measuring muscle protein synthesis rates (e.g., via stable isotope tracers) across morning, afternoon, and evening in older adults under caloric restriction with different protein distributions. — Evaluates the proposed mechanism that evening-skewed protein reduces earlier-day muscle protein synthesis, which could explain the hypothesized impairment.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of existing literature on protein distribution and lean mass outcomes during caloric restriction in older adults. — Aggregates available evidence to assess consistency across studies, potentially confirming or refuting the hypothesis with higher statistical power.

qualifier.comparison: compared to caloric restriction with protein evenly distributed across meals
qualifier.mechanism: Evening-skewed protein may reduce muscle protein synthesis response earlier in the day, negating any benefit of meal timing.

C008.subject: Caloric restriction with protein-matched meal timing

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing daily protein distribution (evenly spread vs. skewed) under caloric restriction in adults aged 65+ with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements of fat-free mass at 0, 6, and 12 months. — Directly tests the hypothesis by isolating the effect of protein-matched meal timing on lean mass retention during caloric restriction, using a gold-standard body composition method over the specified 12-month period.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of intervention studies examining protein timing (e.g., per-meal threshold of ~0.4 g/kg) combined with caloric restriction on lean mass outcomes in older populations. — Aggregates existing evidence to assess consistency and effect size across studies, identifying whether the disputed claim is supported or refuted by the broader literature.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal cohort study using dietary recall and bioelectrical impedance analysis in community-dwelling older adults practicing caloric restriction with varying meal-timing patterns, controlling for total protein intake and physical activity. — Provides observational data in a real-world setting to complement trial findings, capturing long-term adherence and confounding factors that may influence fat-free mass preservation.
